title: Alternaria leaf spot on Edible African Eggplant

Header: Alternaria leaf spot on Edible African Eggplant

Prevention: Use certified seed from a registered distributor
Rotate with non-Solanaceous species such as maize, beans
Remove weeds from within and around the garden
Mix seed with a broad spectrum fungicide before planting
Apply a fungicide spray during transplanting or after the plants have set in the field.
Begin the spraying before leaf spot are seen and continue until harvest
The disease causing organisms do not in the soil on their own except when in the infested host, debris in soil.
Infested debris left on the soil surface can be a significant source of pathogen spores for up to 12 weeks after harvest.
It is therefore important to manage the debris
Monitoring: Monitor the field frequently and look for plants with concentric rings
The spots are mostly irregular, 4-8 mm in diameter and may enlarge and cover a large area of the leaf blade
As soon as symptoms are observed, undertake direct control measures to reduce spread of the disease
Direct Control: Uproot and destroy all infected plants by burning or burying deep (50 cm below ground)
